sample_unit: ED patient cases sampled for physician pre-AI vs post-AI prediction
models_evaluated: Bayesian neural network-based AI bacteremia prediction model (AI-BPM)

links.outcome: Physician AUC for bacteremia prediction before vs after seeing AI output
links.effect: Post-AI physician AUC 0.703 (95% CI 0.654-0.753) vs pre-AI 0.639 (0.585-0.693); p<0.001, in sampled dataset N=1,000. Largest gains when physician uncertainty high and AI uncertainty low.
links.quote: The AUC of the post-AI physicians predictions (0.703, 95% CI 0.654-0.753) was significantly improved compared with that of the pre-AI predictions (0.639, 95% CI 0.585-0.693; p-value < 0.001) in the sampled dataset (N = 1,000).

links.outcome: Model discrimination on temporal and external validation datasets
links.effect: Temporal validation (N=8,188) AUC 0.754; external validation (N=7,029) AUC 0.738, sensitivity 0.927, specificity 0.319; modest drop at external site.
links.quote: In the external validation dataset (N = 7,029), the AI-BPM's AUC was 0.738 (95% CI 0.722-0.755), sensitivity was 0.927 (95% CI 0.909-0.942), and specificity was 0.319 (95% CI 0.307-0.330).

unlisted_practices: Displaying model prediction uncertainty (Bayesian 95% CI relative to risk threshold) to physicians and assessing its interaction with physician confidence

screen.reason: Evaluated the impact of providing AI bacteremia predictions with uncertainty intervals on physician predictions across different levels of AI and clinician uncertainty.

primary.practice: AI uncertainty quantification presentation to clinicians
